source: ASAM OpenDRIVE 1.7.0 (local HTML) chapters 11-13, compared with 1.9.0 online chapters 13-15, Annex F rules and revision histories 1.8/1.9; enumerations cross-checked with tests/xsd/opendrive_1_8_1
annexF_organisation: Annex F (1.9) lists about 275 checker rules grouped by element (F.1-F.6, e.g. F.6.16 object, F.6.19 signal). UID = asam.net:xodr:<version first introduced>:<rule_set path>.<rule_name>. There is no severity field; the text says shall/should/may. Counts: road.object.* 59, road.corner_* 10, road.curve_local.* 5, road.signal.* 20, road.railroad.* 9. Typos are part of the UIDs (validty, surfacees, 1.x.0).

sections.title: Objects - introduction and <object>
sections.summary: Objects are items that expand, delimit or supplement a road (parking spaces, crosswalks, barriers, buildings, trees, poles). Each object belongs to exactly one <road> (inside <road>/<objects>), is placed at an origin (s,t,zOffset) in that road's reference-line frame, and is rotated by hdg/pitch/roll into a local u/v/z frame. Its extent is an angular box (length,width,height) or a cylinder (radius,height). An <outline> (or 1.8+ <skeleton>) refines and supersedes the box but must stay inside it. Objects never move: 'dynamic' only means they have moving parts, such as tunnel fans or wind turbines.
concepts: object = static road furniture tied to one road (road-relative, not inertial)
angular bounding box (length/width/height) vs circular (radius/height) - mutually exclusive, chosen by which attributes are present
local u/v/z frame (spec 6.4): u forward (= s at hdg 0), v left (= t), z up; rotations applied heading -> pitch (about v') -> roll (about u'')
orientation (+/-/none) is traffic-direction validity only; it does NOT rotate the object (hdg does)
validLength: extent of validity along s (0 = point object)
perpToRoad=true makes the object follow the road surface normal and ignores pitch/roll (new in 1.7)
dynamic=yes: object has movable parts but fixed position
only small objects may rely on a single insertion point on a curved elevation (Figure 90)
1.7 axis caveat: 1.7 table text says length along v and width along u; 1.9 corrects this to length along u (forward) and width along v (lateral). Use the 1.9 meaning.

attributes.name: id
attributes.meaning: unique id within the whole file

attributes.name: s
attributes.meaning: s of object origin on the parent road

attributes.name: t
attributes.meaning: t of object origin (lateral from reference line, not from laneOffset)

attributes.name: zOffset
attributes.meaning: origin height relative to reference-line elevation at s

attributes.name: type
attributes.meaning: category. 1.7/1.8 XSD values: none, obstacle, pole, tree, vegetation, barrier, building, parkingSpace, patch, railing, trafficIsland, crosswalk, streetLamp, gantry, soundBarrier, roadMark, roadSurface(1.8), plus deprecated car, van, bus, trailer, bike, motorbike, tram, train, pedestrian, wind. 1.8 deprecates patch->roadSurface, railing/soundBarrier->barrier, streetLamp/wind->pole

attributes.name: subtype
attributes.meaning: variant of type (1.8+ defines subtype tables, e.g. barrier/guardRail, pole/trafficLight, crosswalk/zebra, roadMark/arrowLeft)

attributes.name: dynamic
attributes.meaning: yes = has movable parts; default no

attributes.name: orientation
attributes.meaning: + valid for travel in +s, - for -s, none for both; does not affect heading. Use +/- only if the object affects traffic rules

attributes.name: hdg
attributes.meaning: heading relative to road direction at s (0 = along +s)

attributes.name: pitch
attributes.meaning: pitch relative to x/y plane, applied after hdg

attributes.name: roll
attributes.meaning: roll relative to x/y plane, applied after pitch

attributes.name: perpToRoad
attributes.meaning: true: object perpendicular to road surface everywhere, pitch/roll ignored; default false

attributes.name: length
attributes.meaning: bounding-box extent along local u (1.9 wording; 1.7 text says v)

attributes.name: width
attributes.meaning: bounding-box extent along local v (1.9 wording; 1.7 text says u)

attributes.name: height
attributes.meaning: bounding-box extent along local z, upward from origin

attributes.name: radius
attributes.meaning: cylinder radius in u/v; alternative to length+width

attributes.name: validLength
attributes.meaning: validity along s; 0 for point object

attributes.name: invalidated
attributes.meaning: 1.9 only: physically invalidated (e.g. crossed out); traffic should ignore; default false

attributes.name: temporary
attributes.meaning: 1.9 only: temporary placement (road works); default false

formulas.name: object origin (inertial)
formulas.expr: x0 = xr(s) - t*sin(th(s)); y0 = yr(s) + t*cos(th(s)); z0 = zr(s) + zOffset
formulas.vars: xr,yr,th = reference-line point and heading at s (planView); zr = elevation profile at s; t = lateral offset from the reference line
formulas.notes: t is NOT shifted by laneOffset. In 1.7 zOffset is relative to reference-line elevation; superelevation/shape are not included. On a superelevated road, the surface height at t differs from zr(s), so a writer that wants objects on the surface must add that difference to zOffset itself.

formulas.name: object world heading
formulas.expr: H = th(s) + hdg; then pitch about v', then roll about u''
formulas.vars: th(s) road heading at s, hdg object attribute
formulas.notes: heading 0 = object u-axis along +s. Rotation R = Rz(H)*Ry(pitch)*Rx(roll), ISO 8855 right-handed (u fwd, v left, z up)

formulas.name: local -> inertial
formulas.expr: [x,y,z] = [x0,y0,z0] + Rz(H)*Ry(pitch)*Rx(roll)*[u,v,z]
formulas.vars: u,v,z local coords of a box corner, cornerLocal or vertexLocal
formulas.notes: with perpToRoad=true, replace pitch/roll by the road-surface orientation (slope + superelevation) at (s,t)

formulas.name: angular bounding box
formulas.expr: u in [-length/2,+length/2], v in [-width/2,+width/2], z in [0,height]
formulas.notes: 1.7 has no explicit formula. Centring the box on the origin in u/v, with z from 0 to height, is a common tool convention, not normative; document the choice.

formulas.name: cylinder
formulas.expr: u^2+v^2 <= radius^2, z in [0,height]
formulas.notes: circular object

rules.text: The object's category is given in @type.
An object is either dynamic or static (1.9: it can never change position, heading, pitch or roll).
Do not mix objects derived from ASAM OpenSCENARIO with objects described in OpenDRIVE.
The travel direction for which the object is valid must be specified (@orientation).
The object origin is given in s/t coordinates of its road.
Circular (radius) and angular (length/width) shapes are mutually exclusive; the attributes used define the shape.
Objects placed via elevation/lateral profiles should be small enough not to cut into or float above the road surface, and not to skew OpenCRG surfaces.
If an outline exists, it supersedes the bounding box, but all its points must lie inside the box.
1.9: missing @temporary/@invalidated default to false; traffic actors should ignore invalidated objects.

use_cases.how: type=building; origin at the footprint centroid projected to the nearest road (s,t); hdg = principal-axis angle minus road heading; length/width/height from the oriented bounding box and the height/levels tags; closed <outline> of <cornerLocal> (u,v relative to origin, CCW) with height; orientation=none.
type=tree (1.8+ subtype leaf/needle), radius + height cylinder; 1.8+ optional <skeleton> with trunk and crown polylines; orientation=none.
type=pole (1.8 subtype bollard), radius+height, orientation=none.
type=obstacle with subtype; small radius or box.
type=gantry, box covering the span. Signals sit on it via signal <reference elementType='object'>; 1.8+ can also use boards and a skeleton.

right: Give every object a file-unique id and a @type
Use orientation='none' for non-regulatory objects (buildings, trees, barriers)
Give hdg relative to the road heading at the object's s, not as an absolute inertial heading
Keep outline/skeleton points inside the declared bounding box
Keep s within [0, road length]
wrong: Using orientation to rotate the object (it only states traffic validity)
Supplying radius together with length/width
Using deprecated types (car, streetLamp, railing, soundBarrier, patch) when targeting 1.8+
Placing a large object (building) with perpToRoad on a sloped or curved road
Putting inertial x/y into s/t
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.8: new type roadSurface; patch->roadSurface, railing/soundBarrier->barrier, streetLamp->pole deprecated; per-type subtype and allowed-combination tables (1.9 section 13.14)
1.8: <skeleton> as an alternative or addition to outlines
1.8: 'bounding box' becomes 'bounding volume'; each face should touch the object
1.9: @invalidated, @temporary on <object>
1.9: length/width axis wording corrected (length along u, width along v)
figures: Figure 88: angular vs circular object. Every object is bounded by a box (length,width,height) or a cylinder (radius,height).
Figure 89: UML for objects. <objects> holds object, objectReference, tunnel and bridge; object holds repeat, outlines, material, validity, parkingSpace, markings, borders and surface.

Figure 90: a long straight object inserted at one point on a curved elevation profile cuts into and floats above the road. Only small objects may rely on the insertion point; long ones need a repeat or cornerRoad outlines.

sections.title: Repeating objects
sections.summary: <repeat> clones an object along the road: discrete instances every 'distance' metres, or, with distance=0, one continuous extruded feature (guard rail, wall). Start/end values for t, zOffset, width, height, length and radius are linearly interpolated over the repeat length. Values given in <repeat> override the parent object's; omitted ones are inherited. The schema allows several <repeat> sections per object.
concepts: discrete repeat (distance>0): instances at s+k*distance
continuous repeat (distance=0): extrude the cross-section along the road
linear interpolation of xxxStart/xxxEnd
repeat attributes override object attributes; omitted ones inherit
repeat follows reference-line curvature (1.8 detachFromReferenceLine=true -> straight chord)
1.9: cubic t(ds) via bT/cT/dT

attributes.name: s
attributes.meaning: start s of the repeat area; overrides object @s

attributes.name: length
attributes.meaning: length of the repeat area along s

attributes.name: tStart
attributes.meaning: t of object reference point at s

attributes.name: detachFromReferenceLine
attributes.meaning: 1.8: true = run straight from start to end instead of following the reference line; default false

formulas.name: interpolated attribute
formulas.expr: a(ds) = aStart + (aEnd - aStart) * ds / length,  ds in [0,length]
formulas.vars: a = t, zOffset, width, height, length, radius; ds = distance from repeat @s along the reference line
formulas.notes: stated explicitly in 1.9; implied in 1.7 by the Start/End naming and Figure 91

formulas.name: 1.9 cubic lateral
formulas.expr: t(ds) = tStart + bT*ds + cT*ds^2 + dT*ds^3, with t(length) == tEnd
formulas.vars: bT,cT,dT default 0 (then linear from tStart to tEnd)
formulas.notes: 1.9 only

formulas.name: discrete instance positions
formulas.expr: s_k = s + k*distance, k = 0..floor(length/distance)
formulas.notes: 1.9: no partial instance past s+length; each instance origin lies in [s, s+length] (inclusive), but its volume may overhang. Each instance takes the road heading at s_k plus the object hdg.

formulas.name: continuous feature
formulas.expr: swept cross-section: lateral [t(ds) - width(ds)/2, t(ds) + width(ds)/2], vertical [zr + zOffset(ds), zr + zOffset(ds) + height(ds)], ds in [0,length]
formulas.notes: guard rail / wall / hedge

rules.text: Parameters of the repeated object may differ from the original object.
Repeat parameters override the original object's; omitted ones come from the object.
1.9: repeat s and length must be valid (inside the road).
1.9: a repeated object that has an outline must use <cornerLocal>.
1.9: widthStart/End do not apply to radius-shaped objects.
1.9: length/width/heightStart/End do not apply to objects with outlines or a skeleton; those cannot change size.
Objects with a <surface> CRG may repeat discretely but not continuously.

use_cases.how: type=barrier (1.8 subtype guardRail; 1.7 often 'railing' or 'barrier'), <repeat distance=0 s=.. length=.. tStart/tEnd=edge t heightStart/End=0.75 widthStart/End=0.3>, orientation=none.
type=pole (1.8 subtype streetLamp; 1.7 type streetLamp), one object plus <repeat distance=30..60>.
type=barrier, continuous repeat with height; 1.8 detachFromReferenceLine for straight runs that should not follow the road curve.

use_cases.case: OSM fence diverging from the road
use_cases.how: tStart != tEnd (linear), or 1.9 bT..dT, or split into several repeat sections

right: Use distance=0 for linear features and distance>0 for instances
Give both Start and End values when the feature changes along s
Split a barrier that crosses road boundaries into one repeat per road
wrong: Setting length beyond the road end
Expecting a partial last instance
Using xxxStart/End size changes with outlines
Emitting hundreds of separate objects instead of one repeat
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.8: detachFromReferenceLine
1.9: bT/cT/dT cubic lateral path; explicit placement rules (floor, no partial instance); explicit linear interpolation formula; 4 new checker rules
figures: Figure 91: one large angular object repeated continuously. The top view shows s, length, tStart, tEnd, widthStart and widthEnd following the curve; the side view shows zOffsetStart/End and heightStart/End. Lesson: each Start/End pair interpolates linearly over ds.
Figure 92: several smaller angular objects spaced by distance
Figure 93: several smaller circular objects (radiusStart/End)

sections.title: Object outline (outlines, cornerRoad, cornerLocal)
sections.summary: An <outline> is a polygon or polyline of corner points with per-corner heights. It is used for traffic islands, irregular parking spaces, special markings and buildings. Corners are either all <cornerRoad> (s,t,dz in road coordinates) or all <cornerLocal> (u,v,z in the object's local frame), with at least two per outline. Several outlines per object are allowed via <outlines> (tree trunk + crown, pole + lamp head, logical sub-areas of an island). Readers must still accept a 1.4-style <outline> placed directly under <object>.
concepts: closed=true -> area, else line feature
counter-clockwise order for areas
outer vs inner outlines (holes / sub-areas)
fillType: grass, concrete, cobble, asphalt, pavement, gravel, soil; 1.8 adds paint
laneType: how the application treats the area (e.g. sidewalk, border)
the outline supersedes the bounding box but must fit inside it
cornerRoad: road-relative points that follow curvature; good for shapes along the road
cornerLocal: rigid shape relative to object origin + hdg; good for buildings and islands
outline/corner ids are needed for markings and borders (cornerReference, outlineId)

elements.name: <outlines>
elements.notes: wrapper; 1.4 files may have <outline> directly under <object>

attributes.name: id
attributes.meaning: unique within the object; referenced by <border @outlineId>

attributes.name: outer
attributes.meaning: true = outer outline (1.9: default true, exactly one outer)

attributes.name: closed
attributes.meaning: true = area (last point connects to the first)

attributes.name: laneType
attributes.meaning: lane type the application should treat the area as

attributes.name: dz
attributes.meaning: corner base height relative to reference-line elevation

attributes.name: id
attributes.meaning: unique within the outline; needed if markings reference it

formulas.name: cornerRoad to inertial
formulas.expr: x = xr(s_i) - t_i*sin(th(s_i)); y = yr(s_i) + t_i*cos(th(s_i)); zBase = zr(s_i) + dz_i; zTop = zBase + height_i
formulas.notes: object hdg/pitch/roll do NOT apply to cornerRoad points

formulas.name: cornerLocal to inertial
formulas.expr: [x,y,zBase] = O + Rz(th(s)+hdg) * [u_i, v_i, z_i] (pitch/roll also applied if non-zero); zTop = zBase + height_i
formulas.notes: Figure 96 example: P(s=20, t=-30, zOffset=0), hdg=7pi/4

formulas.name: edge interpolation (explicit in 1.9)
formulas.expr: q(p) = q_i + (q_{i+1}-q_i)*p, p in [0,1], computed in inertial coordinates (cornerRoad) or local coordinates (cornerLocal)
formulas.notes: cornerRoad edges are straight in x/y, NOT curved along the road, so add corners on curves

formulas.name: polygon orientation check
formulas.expr: signedArea = 0.5*sum(x_i*y_{i+1} - x_{i+1}*y_i) > 0 means CCW
formulas.notes: reverse the corner order if negative

rules.text: An <outline> contains one or more <cornerRoad> or one or more <cornerLocal> elements (1.9 also allows <curveLocal>).
Points of an area outline are listed counter-clockwise.
Readers must still support 1.4-style outlines without the <outlines> wrapper.
An outline may be an area or a line. An area may be filled with a fillType. An outline may be outer or inner and may carry a laneType.
All outline points lie inside the object's bounding box.
At least two <cornerRoad> per outline.
No mixing of cornerRoad and cornerLocal (and, in 1.9, curveLocal) in one outline.
At least two <cornerLocal> per outline.
No cornerRoad next to a cornerLocal in the same outline (Annex F gives this UID a placeholder version).
Outline id is unique per object; corner id is unique per outline.
1.9: exactly one outline with outer=true per object (omitted = true).
1.9: where an inner outline touches the outer one, the shared point must be identical.
1.9: corner @id is mandatory if the outline has <markings>.
1.9: same for cornerLocal.
1.9: the first corner id should be 0.
1.9: corner ids should increase by 1 in listing order.
1.9: the first cornerLocal id should be 0.
1.9: cornerLocal ids should increase by 1.

use_cases.how: type=crosswalk, length/width box, closed outline of 4 cornerRoad points spanning the carriageway (s +/- half the crossing width, t from the outer edge on one side to the other), stripes via marking + cornerReference (11.6). For pedestrian simulation in 1.8+, also model the walking path as a <crossPath> in a junction.
type=trafficIsland, closed outer outline (cornerRoad if aligned with the road, else cornerLocal), fillType=grass/pavement, <borders><border type='curb' width='0.15' outlineId='0'/> (11.7).
type=parkingSpace, closed cornerRoad/cornerLocal outline (rectangular or rhomboid), <parkingSpace access=...>, markings on the sides.
type=building, closed outline of cornerLocal with constant height, outer=true; courtyards as inner outlines (outer=false).

type=roadMark (1.8 subtype signalLines), a thin closed outline across the lanes with <validity> for the affected lanes. Give it regulatory meaning with a stop-line signal referenced from the sign or light (12.3).

right: Use CCW order and closed=true for areas
Add cornerRoad points on curves (edges are straight lines)
Number ids from 0 consecutively
Make the bounding box enclose every outline point
Use cornerLocal for shapes defined by footprint geometry (OSM polygons)
wrong: Mixing cornerRoad and cornerLocal in one outline
Only one corner
Outline points outside the bounding box
Applying the object hdg to cornerRoad points
Clockwise polygons for areas

1.9: exactly-one-outer and id rules; curve continuity (road.curve_local.continuous_curve_local), length_match, paramPoly3 range rules
1.9: markings of outlined objects move inside <outline> (see 11.6)
1.9: default 'closed' per object type given in the 13.14 tables (mostly true)
figures: Figure 94: traffic island modelled as an object with an outline (and logical sub-areas)
Figure 95: non-linear object built from cornerRoad s/t points; the corners follow the road frame

Figure 96: object built from cornerLocal. Origin P(s=20, t=-30, zOffset=0) is projected from the road, hdg=7pi/4, and corners [u1,v1]..[u9,v9] lie in the rotated local frame. Lesson: cornerLocal is rigid relative to origin + hdg, independent of road curvature.

sections.title: Object material
sections.summary: <material> gives an object (for example a patch in the road surface) its own surface code, friction and roughness, overriding the road material inside the object's outline. The values are application-defined. 1.8 adds roadMarkColor for painted objects.
concepts: material overrides <road>/lane material only inside the object's outline
surface/friction/roughness are application-specific

attributes.name: roadMarkColor
attributes.meaning: 1.8: colour of painted markings (standard, blue, green, red, white, yellow, black(1.8), orange, violet)

rules.text: An object's material may differ from the surrounding road.

use_cases.case: asphalt patch / cobbled area in a road
use_cases.how: type=roadSurface (1.8; 1.7 patch) with an outline and <material surface='cobble' friction='0.6'/>

use_cases.case: painted area (bus lane colour, crosswalk paint)
use_cases.how: 1.8: outline fillType='paint' + material roadMarkColor='red'

right: Use material only together with an outline/area
wrong: Expecting material to change the lane's own material outside the object

sections.title: Lane validity for objects
sections.summary: By default an object applies to all lanes. <validity fromLane toLane> limits it to a lane-id range, and several elements may be given. @orientation (direction) and <validity> (lanes) complement each other and are not interchangeable; both should be used only for traffic-rule-relevant objects such as stop-line outlines.
concepts: orientation = travel direction, validity = lane set
validity range must be consistent with orientation and traffic hand
use +/- orientation and validity only for objects that matter for traffic rules

attributes.name: fromLane
attributes.meaning: lowest lane id the item applies to

attributes.name: toLane
attributes.meaning: highest lane id the item applies to (fromLane <= toLane)

attributes.name: layer
attributes.meaning: 1.9 only: lane layer (default 'permanent'); valid on both permanent and temporary layers needs two <validity> elements

formulas.name: RHT consistency
formulas.expr: orientation '+' => all [fromLane,toLane] < 0 ; '-' => all > 0 ; mixed => orientation 'none'
formulas.vars: lane ids of the parent road
formulas.notes: LHT: swap the signs

formulas.name: lane membership
formulas.expr: valid(lane) = OR_k (from_k <= lane <= to_k)
formulas.notes: lane 0 (centre lane) can technically be inside a range spanning both signs

rules.text: An object may be valid for selected lanes, or for one lane only.
The lanes covered by all <validity> elements must fall inside the parent's @orientation.
RHT: orientation '+' -> validity only on negative lane ids; '-' -> only positive ids; both signs -> orientation must be 'none'.
LHT: orientation '-' -> only negative ids; '+' -> only positive ids; both signs -> 'none'.
fromLane <= toLane.
Use orientation '+'/'-' only if the object affects traffic rules, otherwise 'none'; use <validity> only for traffic-rule-relevant objects (e.g. stop-line outlines).

use_cases.how: object roadMark with orientation='+' and <validity fromLane='-2' toLane='-1'/>

use_cases.case: tunnel or bridge that covers only some lanes
use_cases.how: <validity> child of <tunnel>/<bridge>

right: Check sign consistency against the header's traffic hand (rule=RHT/LHT in road @rule)
wrong: orientation='+' with validity on positive lanes in RHT
fromLane > toLane

sections.title: Access rules to parking spaces
sections.summary: A parking space is a normal <object type='parkingSpace'> whose outline (cornerRoad/cornerLocal) gives its shape (rectangular or rhomboid). An optional <parkingSpace> child restricts access to a group of users or vehicles and can carry free-text restrictions.
concepts: shape via outline; access via <parkingSpace>
women/handicapped spaces imply vehicle type car

attributes.name: access
attributes.meaning: all, car, women, handicapped, bus, truck, electric, residents (required in 1.9 table)

rules.text: Access to a parking space may be limited to a group of persons or vehicles.
Further restrictions may be defined but are outside OpenDRIVE.

use_cases.how: type=parkingSpace, closed outline per bay, <parkingSpace access='all'/>, side markings (11.6); repeat with cornerLocal for regular bays
access='handicapped'

right: Combine with markings for the painted bay lines
wrong: Using lane type parking alone when individual bays are needed
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.8/1.9: parkingSpace subtypes openSpace/closedSpace; 13.14 table: width/length mandatory, radius not allowed, outline optional (closed default true)
figures: Figure 97: rectangular and rhomboid parking spaces described by outline corners

sections.title: Object marking
sections.summary: <markings>/<marking> describe painted lines belonging to an object (crosswalk stripes, stop lines, parking bay lines). A marking runs either along one side of the bounding box (@side) or as straight lines between referenced outline corners (<cornerReference id>). It is a dashed pattern given by lineLength and spaceLength, with width, colour and thickness (zOffset).
concepts: bounding-box mode: side=left/right/front/rear + start/stopOffset
outline mode: cornerReference ids form the polyline
dash pattern lineLength/spaceLength (spaceLength 0 = solid)
marking zOffset = paint thickness above road

attributes.name: startOffset
attributes.meaning: offset along u from the start of the box side to the first dash

attributes.name: stopOffset
attributes.meaning: offset from the end of the box side where the marking stops

attributes.name: side
attributes.meaning: left/right/front/rear side of the bounding box (local u/v)

attributes.name: id
attributes.meaning: id of a referenced outline corner

formulas.name: dash positions on a side or segment
formulas.expr: for a segment of length L: d_k = startOffset + k*(lineLength+spaceLength), dash = [d_k, min(d_k+lineLength, L - stopOffset)] while d_k < L - stopOffset
formulas.vars: L = side length (length or width) or the distance between referenced corners
formulas.notes: 1.7 gives no algorithm; this is the natural reading. Each dash is a rectangle of 'width' centred on the line.

rules.text: The marking of an object is defined completely or partially on its outline (1.9: complete_or_partial_on_outline).
The marking colour must be defined.
Without an outline, @side is mandatory.
With an outline, at least two <cornerReference> are mandatory (1.9: or one curveLocal reference).
Without an outline, <cornerReference> must not be used.
1.9: without outlines, <markings> sit in <object>.
1.9: with outlines, <markings> sit inside the <outline>.
1.9: a marking going all round a closed outline repeats the first id at the end (two cornerReferences with the same id).
1.9: corners between non-consecutive referenced corners must also be listed.
1.9: cornerReference ids follow the outline's point order.

use_cases.how: object type=crosswalk + closed cornerRoad outline (ids 0..3); two <marking> elements referencing corners 0-1 and 2-3 (edge lines) as in the 1.7 example (width 0.1, white, lineLength 0.2, spaceLength 0.05). Alternatively, for zebra bars: front/rear side marking with lineLength=bar width, spaceLength=gap, width=crossing length.
roadMark object with marking side='front' and width 0.3-0.5, or a closed outline with fillType='paint' (1.8)
markings on the left/right/front sides of a parkingSpace box

right: Use ids on corners referenced by markings
Keep marking zOffset small (a few mm)
wrong: Using @side and cornerReference together
Omitting colour
Referencing corner ids that do not exist
changes_1_8_1_9: 1.9: markings of outlined objects move into <outline>; ordering, enclosure and between-points rules; closed outline + fillType=paint for filled painted areas
figures: Figure 98: crosswalk trapezoid defined by cornerRoad s1=5, s2=8, s3=12, s4=15 with t=+/-3.5. The dashed slanted edge lines are markings referencing corners 0-1 and 2-3. Lesson: marking lines follow straight corner-to-corner segments.

sections.title: Object borders
sections.summary: <borders>/<border> add a frame of given width and type (concrete, curb; 1.8 paint) along an outline, for example the curb of a traffic island. The frame follows the whole outline, or only the referenced corners when useCompleteOutline=false.
concepts: border = frame along outline

sections.title: Signals - introduction and <signal>
sections.summary: Signals are traffic signs, traffic lights and regulatory road markings that control traffic. Each <signal> sits in <road>/<signals> at (s,t) relative to that road. Its zOffset is the height of its bottom edge, its orientation names the traffic direction it applies to, and hOffset turns its face. It is identified by country + countryRevision + type + subtype (+ value/unit). Signals override other traffic rules, can be static or dynamic (traffic lights, with state from OpenSCENARIO), and must be placed so that the road, lanes and start of validity are unambiguous. Non-binding road marks are objects, not signals.

height/width recommended for rendering

sections.title: Railroads - introduction
sections.summary: OpenDRIVE models trams and streetcars only where rails meet roads; it does not cover complex rail networks or rail signalling. Rails live on roads: each track is its own <road>, and <road>/<railroad> holds switches. In 1.9, switches are the only rail-specific element; tracks use <road> and signals use <signal>.
concepts: one road per track
<railroad> container in <road>

rules.text: Each railway track requires its own road (one tram/rail lane per road).

use_cases.how: separate <road> for the tram track along the street centre, lane type 'tram'; the street road stays separate

1.7: model as a junction or overlapping roads; 1.8+: <junction type='crossing'> with <roadSection roadId sStart sEnd> per road (rules junctions.crossing.only_road_sections, only_one_high_prio, s_start_end_coverage)

right: Keep tram tracks out of road lanes
wrong: A tram lane inside a car road

sections.title: Railroad tracks
sections.summary: A track is a road whose single lane has type 'rail' or 'tram'. Its reference line runs along the centre of the rail pair (use laneOffset so the lane centre lies on the reference line), and the lane is at least as wide as the vehicle.
concepts: reference line = track centreline
lane type rail/tram
laneOffset shifts the lane so it is centred

formulas.name: centred rail lane
formulas.expr: laneOffset = w/2 with a single right lane -1 of width w (Figure 114)
formulas.notes: the lane then spans t in [-w/2,+w/2]

rules.text: The reference line lies in the centre of the rail pair.
Only one tram or rail lane per road.
The lane is at least as wide as the rail vehicles.

use_cases.how: road with lane -1 type tram, width 2.65, laneOffset 1.325

right: Centre the reference line on the track
wrong: Reference line at the lane edge as for roads
figures: Figure 114: road reference line at the lane edge vs railway reference line centred via laneOffset

sections.title: Switches (mainTrack, sideTrack, partner)
sections.summary: <switch> on a track's <railroad> splits it into two directions. It is dynamic (operable during simulation) or static (fixed 'straight' or 'turn'). <mainTrack id s dir> gives the switch point on the main track; <sideTrack id s dir> gives the branch road. Two switches joined by a side track are partners and must be set consistently.
concepts: switch = 2-way split (unlike junctions)
mainTrack = this road; sideTrack connects two switches
partner switches share a side track

attributes.name: id
attributes.meaning: road id of main track (must be the parent road)

attributes.name: dir
attributes.meaning: +/-: direction on main track to enter the side track

attributes.name: s
attributes.meaning: s of switch on side track

attributes.name: dir
attributes.meaning: direction on side track after entering

rules.text: A switch may be dynamic or static.
Main tracks shall not be used to connect two switches.
Side tracks link two switches only.
Partner switches indicate that a side track links two switches.
Single switches have no partner.
Switch connections must be consistent (Annex F).

sections.title: Stations, platforms, segments
sections.summary: A top-level <station> (tram or bus) has at least one <platform>, and each platform has at least one <segment roadId sStart sEnd side>. The segments tie the platform to track or road stretches and give the side of the track it is on.
concepts: station at OpenDRIVE level (like junctions)
platform = physical extent
segment = road s-range + side

attributes.name: side
attributes.meaning: left | right, seen from sStart to sEnd

rules.text: At least one platform per station.
Each platform is referenced by >=1 track.
A platform contains >=1 segment.
>=1 segment per platform.
